chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from Abd al-A'la said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Hady (sacrificial animal for Hajj) except from camels, and no slaughter except at Mina.' And all of Mina is a place of slaughter, and the best of it is the Mosque. He narrated that.

key_terms.إِبِل: Camels (specifically mentioned as the type for Hady)
key_terms.اَلْمَسْجِد: The Mosque (specifically Masjid al-Haram or the mosque in Mina)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the location near Mecca where Hajj rituals take place
key_terms.هَدْي: Hady, the sacrificial animal offered during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the Hady sacrifice during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies that the Hady (sacrificial animal) for Hajj must be from camels and its slaughter must take place in Mina. He clarifies that the entire area of Mina is considered a valid place for slaughter, with the Mosque in Mina being the most preferable location. This ruling reflects the specific jurisprudential interpretation within the Shia tradition regarding the type of animal and the sanctity of the slaughter site, distinguishing it from general sacrificial practices.
